raw_findings.message: Content-Length is trusted without a size limit, allowing a client to make a handler read an arbitrarily large body or tie up a thread while sending it slowly.
The mutating handlers do not read or verify X-Owner, so a caller can transfer from or close an account belonging to another owner by supplying its ID.
The user-controlled account label is interpolated into HTML without escaping, so a label containing markup or script executes when its statement page is viewed.
Client-supplied fields are assigned directly to the Account object, allowing a caller to set protected attributes such as balance_cents, closed, or id and thereby mint funds or corrupt account state.
Transfers do not check whether either account is closed, so funds can still be sent from or into an account after it has been closed.
The funds check covers only the transfer amount, not the amount plus FEE_CENTS, so transferring the entire balance succeeds and leaves the source overdrawn.
Negative amounts pass can_cover and are applied as reverse transfers without checking the destination's balance, so a caller can drain another account into their own.
Concurrent transfers can read the same source and house balances before either updates them, causing lost debits or fees while both destinations receive funds.
The destination is checked only after the source is debited and the fee is credited, so transferring to an unknown account returns an error after changing balances.

fixed_raw_findings.message: Ownership checks trust the client-supplied X-Owner value without authenticating it, so a caller who can reach the service can claim another owner's identity and access or mutate that owner's accounts.

Account creation accepts caller-chosen initial balances without debiting any source or binding creation to an authorized identity, so repeated requests can create arbitrary funds up to the per-account cap.
The upper-bound-only clamp accepts negative initial_cents, allowing accounts to start with negative balances and closing one to reduce the house balance.

Closing an account does not acquire the lock used by transfers, so a concurrent transfer can pass its checks while the close moves the balance and marks the account closed, then debit the closed account and credit the destination.

raw_findings.message: No route verifies the caller's X-Owner identity or account ownership, so any caller that can reach the service can read other accounts and transfer funds or close accounts.
The user-controlled account label is inserted into HTML without escaping, so a label containing markup or script executes when the HTML statement is viewed.
The request fields are copied onto the Account after its ID and capped balance are set, allowing a caller to assign an arbitrary balance or ID and, for example, overwrite the house account.
Transfers do not check whether either account is closed, so a closed account can still send or receive funds after being closed.
The balance check covers only the transfer amount and not the fee, so transferring an entire balance succeeds and leaves the source account negative by the fee.
Negative amounts pass the balance check and cause the source to gain funds while the destination is debited, so a caller can create an invalid transfer and distort account balances.
Concurrent transfers can both read the same source balance before the journal write and sleep, then each credit its destination while only one source debit is reflected.
The destination is checked only after the source and house balances are changed, so a transfer to an unknown account returns an error after still debiting the source and charging the fee.

fixed_raw_findings.message: Content-Length is used to read the entire request body without a size limit, so a caller can exhaust memory or tie up a request thread by sending an excessively large body.
Ownership is authorized solely by comparing X-Owner, which a caller can supply, so a caller can impersonate an account owner and read, transfer from, or close that owner's accounts.
Accounts created without an owner are permanently inaccessible because this check rejects every request when acc.owner is empty, potentially trapping any initial balance in such an account.
Negative initial_cents values are accepted, creating accounts with negative balances that violate the ledger's balance invariants and can propagate negative funds when closed.
Account ownership is taken directly from the request body rather than the caller's authenticated identity, so a caller can create accounts that appear under another owner's identity.

The close operation permits closing HOUSE_ID, so a caller authorized as the house can close the shared fee account and cause all subsequent transfers to fail because transfers reject closed destinations.

raw_findings.message: Content-Length is trusted without a size limit, allowing clients to make server threads read arbitrarily large bodies and consume excessive memory or remain occupied.
Account listings and statements are served without owner checks, exposing every account's owner, label, balance, and transaction history to any client.
Transfer and close operations never validate the X-Owner header or account ownership, so any client able to reach the service can move funds from or close another owner's account.
The account label is interpolated into HTML without escaping, so a label containing markup or script is executed when its statement page is viewed.
Negative offsets or limits are accepted as Python slice indices, causing requests to return unintended entries from the end of a statement.

Applying every request field as an account attribute lets a caller override protected fields such as id and balance_cents, bypass the initial-balance cap, or overwrite an existing account including the house account.
Concurrent transfers can both pass the balance check before either updates it, allowing overspending and inconsistent ledger balances.
The funds check ignores the 25-cent fee, so a transfer equal to the source balance succeeds and leaves that account overdrawn by 25 cents.
Negative amounts pass the funds check and let a caller credit the source while debiting the destination, potentially driving another account arbitrarily negative.
The source and house balances are changed before a missing destination is rejected, so a transfer to an unknown account returns an error after still debiting the source and charging the fee.
Transfers do not reject closed accounts, so callers can credit a closed destination and leave funds in an account that has already been closed.

fixed_raw_findings.message: The handler reads the entire declared body without a size limit, so a client can send an oversized body or slowly withhold bytes to consume memory and tie up a server thread.
This iterates the accounts dictionary while account creation can modify it without a shared lock, so a concurrent request can raise a mutation-during-iteration error and return 500.
If owner is omitted or empty, the account is created with an empty owner, which _owned rejects for every caller and can leave any opening funds permanently inaccessible.
Authorization trusts the caller-supplied X-Owner header without independently authenticating it, so a client can impersonate an account owner to read statements, transfer funds, or close accounts.
Only the upper bound is enforced, so a negative initial_cents value creates an account with a negative opening balance.
